title: FACT CHECK: ‘No 2028 election’ claim has no basis
summary: Malacañang, House leaders, and the Commission on Elections dismissed resurfacing claims of a ‘no-el’ (no-election) scenario in 2028

blocks.text: Claim: There will be no national elections in 2028, according to Vice President Sara Duterte’s spokesperson, Paolo Panelo.

Why we fact-checked this: Facebook user Banat by Supporter posted a video narrating details about the supposed ‘no election’ plan. The video has garnered 10,100 reactions, 918 comments, and 660 shares.
He said, “‘No elections sa 2028’ – ‘yan po ang sinabi ni VP Sara Duterte.”
(‘No elections in 2028’ – that is what VP Sara Duterte said.)

“Actually nabanggit na po ito before ni VP Sara… Paano niya nasabi ‘yan? Nung hindi pa si VP Sara Duterte at si Pangulong Bongbong Marcos, sinabi na daw sa kanya ni BBM at sinabihan siya na plano talagang baguhin ang konstitusyon,” he added.

(Actually, VP Sara has already mentioned this before… How could she have said that? Before they became [Vice President] Sara Duterte and President Bongbong Marcos, BBM had already told her — he mentioned to her — that there was a definite plan to amend the Constitution.)
The facts: The 2028 national elections will proceed as planned. There is no official government announcement that says otherwise. Several government officials have also refuted the claim.

Claims about supposed plans to postpone the 2028 polls resurfaced after Panelo said in a November 19 media interview that the Vice President received information of a “no-elections” scenario for the 2028 polls, based on alleged discussions in the House of Representatives.

On November 19, House Senior Deputy Speaker Ferdinand Hernandez dismissed the allegations, saying they had “absolutely no basis.” He added, “There is no such a plan or proposal that is being pushed by the House leadership.”

Lanao del Sur 1st District Representative Zia Alonto Adiong and Manila 3rd District Representative Joel Chua have also said that Duterte’s camp was floating the “no-el” scenario to divert attention from the Vice President’s ongoing impeachment trial at the Senate.
Malacañang likewise dismissed the claim, with Palace Press Officer Claire Castro calling out the Vice President’s camp for “making up” stories.

On November 22, Commission on Elections Chairman George Garcia refuted the claim, saying, “Imposibleng mangyari. Ang Saligang Batas ang nagsasabing may eleksyon sa 2028. Walang kahit na anong batas ang pwedeng gawin ng Kongreso, pirmahan ng pangulo ang makakapagbago sa Saligang Batas.”
(That is impossible. The Constitution mandates that there be an election in 2028. No law enacted by Congress — nor any signed by the President — can alter the Constitution.)

According to Article 7, Section 4 of the 1987 Constitution, a president and a vice president shall be elected by direct vote of the people for a six-year term, with their terms beginning at noon on the 30th day of June of the same election year.

Charter change: Duterte has previously claimed that President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. had been trying to change the Constitution to extend his term. In one of her statements, she said, “The desperation of the administration to bring me down, push for Charter Change, prevent the 2028 elections, and cling to power is becoming increasingly diabolical.”

Marcos has earlier expressed openness to changing the 1987 Constitution’s economic provisions to attract foreign investors, but has repeatedly rejected claims that he is pushing for charter change to extend his presidency.
